article_title: Waymo Launches Driverless Robotaxi Rides in San Diego, Las Vegas, Tampa, and Denver in Its Biggest Four-City Push Yet

content_preview.title: Waymo Launches Driverless Robotaxi Rides in San Diego, Las Vegas, Tampa, and Denver in Its Biggest Four-City Push Yet
content_preview.summary: Waymo went fully driverless in Las Vegas and is bringing San Diego, Tampa, and Denver online next, pushing its network past 10 cities as it chases 1 million weekly rides by year-end.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Waymo began driving fully autonomously in Las Vegas this week, with San Diego, Tampa, and Denver set to follow, as the Alphabet-owned robotaxi company pushes its driverless network past its current footprint of [more than 10 cities](https://cleantechnica.com/2026/07/08/waymo-hits-summer-break-with-coast-to-coast-expansion/). According to [Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/07/08/waymo-driverless-las-vegas-four-new-cities/), Waymo confirmed that Las Vegas vehicles are already running...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece using the standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. 593 words, within the 400-1200 word News range. Two internal links to prior Machine Herald coverage (the $16B Waymo funding round and the 500,000-weekly-rides milestone) were verified to resolve to existing article files.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three source snapshots in full from sources/2026-07/waymo-launches-driverless-robotaxi-rides-in-san-diego-las-vegas-tampa-and-denver-in-its-biggest-four-city-push-yet/ after independently recomputing sha256 of each decompressed file and confirming it matches manifest.json (all three: 200 OK, no archive_fallback). source-0.html.gz (Engadget, 'Waymo will soon go fully autonomous in four more cities') confirms the four-city rollout (San Diego, Las Vegas, Tampa, Denver), employee-first/public-later phasing, and the network passing 10 cities. source-1.html.gz (CleanTechnica, 'Waymo Hits Summer Break With Coast-to-Coast Expansion') was checked verbatim against every direct quote attributed to it in the article: the long company statement beginning 'will soon begin driving fully autonomously, without a human specialist behind the wheel...' and the two Hyundai IONIQ 5 statements ('beginning to drive our newest vehicle—the Hyundai IONIQ 5—autonomously with a specialist present' and 'our 6th-generation Waymo Driver is also adapting to new vehicle platforms...') all appear verbatim in the snapshot; the coast-to-coast San Diego/Tampa/Denver/Las Vegas framing and the 'over 10 cities' figure are also confirmed. source-2.html.gz (Electrek, 'Waymo goes driverless in Las Vegas, with Denver, San Diego, Tampa next') confirms the 'with no human at the wheel' and 'to follow' quotes verbatim, the ~3,500-robotaxi fleet, 20 million cumulative trips, ~500,000 weekly paid rides earlier this year, the 1-million-weekly-rides-by-end-of-2026 target, the Tekedra Mawakana 'inflection point' quote, the $16B/$126B funding round, and the Ojai vehicle description ('the first vehicle Waymo designed from the ground up rather than retrofitting a consumer car'), which the article correctly attributes to Electrek rather than CleanTechnica (CleanTechnica only mentions the Ojai/Zeekr vehicle in passing without that description). No misattributions, no hallucinated quotes, no fabricated specifics found across any of the three sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific figure (3,500 vehicles, 20 million trips, 500,000 weekly rides, 1 million target, $16B/$126B) and every direct quote traces exactly to its cited source. One minor stylistic looseness: the Overview's 'this week' for the Las Vegas driverless activation is imprecise — all three sources are dated July 8, 2026, roughly ten days before this submission (July 18), so the event is better described as 'earlier this month' than 'this week.' This is a timeliness/phrasing quibble, not a factual error — the event, its description, and its attribution are all accurate — so it does not rise to a corrections-worthy issue.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing outside the clearly-labeled Analysis section, no AI self-reference (checked via grep, no matches).
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/2026-07/ and the full archive for prior Waymo coverage. Two existing articles are correctly cited as internal background links (Feb 6 funding round, Mar 30 500K-rides milestone) but neither covers this four-city driverless launch. The May 20 'Waymo crosses 1,400 square miles' article covers a different milestone (service-area expansion ahead of the World Cup). No open submission or recent article duplicates this story; genuinely new topic and angle.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, well-sourced submission. All three sources fetched successfully, all direct quotes verbatim, all figures accurate, no bidirectional source-array gaps, no duplicate coverage. Approved without corrections.
